newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil monopoly to privatise from mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil monopoly to privatise from mid-1997.

text.p: Taiwan's state oil monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Thursday it would begin its long-awaited privatisation as early as July -- a half-year late -- and complete the process on schedule by July 2000.
"Chinese Petroleum will start the process in fiscal year 1997/98," company executive Liao Pei-feng told Reuters by telephone.
The monopoly's fiscal year starts on July 1.
Fifteen percent of company equity would be released in the first year to the local stock market to establish a market price for subsequent stock swaps with foreign oil companies, he said.
The process will be completed in fiscal year 1999/2000, when more than 50 percent of the company will be in private hands.
Vice president Roy Chiu has said the planned stock release would involve a public offering, stock swaps with oil-rich foreign states and sales to major investors.
"The stock swaps are intended to secure Taiwan's oil supply," Chiu told Reuters in a recent interview. "Any firm holding major oil reserves is a likely candidate for a swap."
Officials declined to give details or a timetable for the stock releases, swaps and other aspects of the privatisation.
